summary_html: Youth remains in **extended foster care** or receives **transitional services** after age 18 under federal programs promoting independence.
authority_html:
- **Chafee Foster Care Independence Act (CFCIA)** — independent-living and transition funding  
- **FCSIAA** — extends care to age 21 with education and housing supports

New Hampshire - RSA 169-C:1 et seq. (Procedures for abuse/neglect cases)
New Hampshire - RSA 170-G (Services for Children, Youth and Families – DCYF program authority)

regulations_applicable.title: Fam - Board of Family Mediator Certification

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: On certiorari brought by the child herself, the court held that approving her placement in a residential treatment program without first holding an evidentiary hearing did not violate due process, that several placement challenges were moot, and that the circuit court did not err in denying her requests for records disclosure to her grandmother, placement with her father, or changes to the dispositional order.
key_cases.relevance: The permanency plan was changed to another planned permanent living arrangement once adoption by the grandmother became unavailable, the pathway most often followed by youth who age out.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the court’s approval of K.S.’s placement in an institutional setting without holding an evidentiary hearing did not violate K.S.’s right to due process

key_cases.holding: The court vacated the primary and concurrent case plans because the circuit court rejected reunification as the permanency goal while simultaneously finding reunification remained possible; RSA 169-C:19, III requires the court to identify a legally permissible primary plan before it can identify a concurrent plan, and the matter was remanded for a new dispositional order.
key_cases.relevance: Another planned permanent living arrangement is listed as a permanency option, but only after the reunification determination is properly made.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court cannot identify the concurrent plan without first identifying the primary plan, which, as explained above, requires a preliminary determination of whether reunification is possible

state_agency.name: Division for Children, Youth and Families
state_agency.hotline: 1-800-894-5533 (in-state only) or 603-271-6562; DCYF Central Intake is staffed 24 hours a day, including weekends and holidays

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (HOPE program; voluntary; only if in NH DHHS legal custody at 18; RSA 169-C:34, V-a)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
